definitions: To establish someone in a new business or position.
To provide someone with the money or means to do something.
To trick or deceive someone, often into a compromising situation.
To frame someone for a crime they did not commit.
examples: His parents set him up in a small restaurant.
The lottery win set her up for life.
The police believed someone set him up.
They tried to set me up to take the fall.
pastTenses: set sb up (past simple), has/have set sb up (present perfect)
